title: Artemis I Night Launch - SLS and Orion to the Moon

moments.title: Countdown hold awaiting new T-0
moments.summary: The broadcast opens on the SLS on the pad at night while launch control works upper-stage valve issues and explains launch-window cutouts. Teams await the mission management poll to set a new T-zero.
moments.evidence: speech: 'we are starting to track to a T-zero close to around a quarter till top of the hour' with live pad and firing room views

moments.title: Final go/no-go polls and go to resume count
moments.summary: NASA test director Jeff Spaulding polls the launch team, all stations report go with no constraints. Launch Director Charlie Blackwell-Thompson gives go to resume count and launch Artemis One.
moments.evidence: speech: 'Artemis Generation, this is for you. At this time, I give you a go to resume count and launch Artemis One' then 'Three, two, one, mark'

moments.title: Terminal countdown T-10 minutes to liftoff
moments.summary: The clock counts from T-10 minutes through core-stage pressurization, FTS arming, engine-bleed checks, engine gimbal test, transfer to internal power and handover to autonomous launch sequencer.
moments.evidence: speech: 'T-minus 10 minutes and counting' to 'we are go for ALS. The Space Launch System is now counting down to liftoff of Orion'

moments.title: Engine ignition and liftoff
moments.summary: Hydrogen burnoff igniters fire, the four RS-25 engines start and boosters ignite. Artemis I lifts off the pad in a blaze of light, rising together back to the Moon.
moments.evidence: speech: 'Four stage engine start. Three, two, one. Boosters ignition. And liftoff of Artemis One.'

moments.title: Powered ascent through Max Q
moments.summary: SLS climbs on 8.8 million pounds of thrust, throttling down and back up through Max Q. Houston reports good control and roll while speed builds past 2,800 mph.
moments.evidence: speech: 'Max Q at about one minute and nine seconds' and 'traveling over 2,800 miles per hour'

moments.title: Solid rocket booster separation
moments.summary: About two minutes eleven seconds into flight the twin 177-foot boosters cut off and jettison, leaving the core stage on four RS-25s continuing to power Orion.
moments.evidence: speech: 'Confirmation that the solid rocket boosters have separated' with two plumes moving apart in night sky

moments.title: Service module fairing and LAS separation
moments.summary: Telemetry cameras show the service module fairing panels and launch abort system pyros firing and separating about three minutes into flight as Orion heads to orbit.
moments.evidence: speech: 'confirmation that the service module fairing has separated' and 'launch abort system pyros have fired' on VIS-FOV view

moments.title: Core stage burn to orbit - animation
moments.summary: Animation follows the SLS core stage firing over Earth at up to 12,800+ mph while Houston monitors four good engines toward main engine cutoff at about eight minutes.
moments.evidence: visual: tan SLS core with cyan-blue engine plumes over Earth's night side with timeline LIFTOFF MAX Q SRB SEP

moments.title: MECO and core stage separation
moments.summary: Core stage main engine cutoff is confirmed with Orion in Earth orbit, followed by core stage separation leaving Orion and the ICPS flying free.
moments.evidence: speech: 'Core stage main engine cutoff, Orion is now in Earth's orbit' and call for core stage separation

moments.title: Watching liftoff from Kennedy - hosts react
moments.summary: Hosts Megan and astronaut Kayla Barron describe the night sky lighting up, the ground shaking and the emotional liftoff, then toss to the firing room for the launch director.
moments.evidence: speech: 'it lit up the night sky and it just shook everything' and 'trajectory looked like it was flying towards the moon'

moments.title: Launch director's speech and tie-cut tradition
moments.summary: Launch Director Charlie Blackwell-Thompson tells her team they earned their place in history on the first Artemis launch, then takes part in the tie-cutting tradition and hugs.
moments.evidence: speech: 'You have earned your place in history. You were part of a first. The first launch of Artemis.'

moments.title: Solar array deployment and orbit update
moments.summary: Mission Control Houston tracks Orion and ICPS at 16,000+ mph while four solar arrays are released, unfold live and latch. All four deployed is confirmed as teams look to the perigee raise maneuver.
moments.evidence: speech: 'all four solar arrays have been released' to 'we have confirmation all four arrays are deployed' with live array view

moments.title: Why the Moon - south pole explainer
moments.summary: Presenter Dan Hewitt at the Moon board recaps Apollo, LRO and LCROSS water-ice discoveries, 13 Artemis III south-pole sites and using the Moon to learn to live off the land for Mars.
moments.evidence: visual: large Moon map with Apollo sites and south-pole topography; speech about 'in situ resource utilization' and water for fuel

moments.title: Red crew interview - fixing the hydrogen leak
moments.summary: Trent, Chad and Billy of the red crew describe entering the blast danger zone for the first time to torque down a loose hydrogen valve packing, enabling launch after 37 years of training.
moments.evidence: speech: 'red crew was sent out... small leak on a hydrogen valve' and 'tightened her up' on zero deck with rocket creaking

moments.title: Mission Control update - imagery team
moments.summary: Leah previews the perigee raise and translunar injection burns and introduces the Orion imagery team monitoring cameras that will livestream from the vicinity of the Moon.
moments.evidence: speech: 'about 17 minutes until the perigee raise maneuver' and 'first time live streaming digital video from vicinity of the Moon'

moments.title: CubeSats and science inside Orion
moments.summary: Hosts and scientists explain ten shoebox-size secondary-payload CubeSats, lunar, solar and biology experiments and space radiation studies paving the way for deeper exploration.
moments.evidence: speech: 'inside of Orion are ten CubeSats ... secondary payloads' with model and animations of deploying sails
